analysis.title: Amazon.com Amazon Logistics call: More automation on the way
key_insights: MWPVL (Marc Wulfraat) estimates Amazon's logistics network is nearing full capacity and expects capacity additions to accelerate in 2027, to ~91mn gross sq. ft. from ~66mn in 2026 (+38%).

MWPVL estimates ~$28bn of spend on new supply chain facilities over 2026-2027 (excludes maintenance and retrofits), which could be up $10bn on an annualized basis. Spend is focused on small-sortable robotic fulfillment centers, inbound cross-dock and delivery stations.
Retail logistics capex is small against BofA's $240bn estimate for 2027 AWS capex, but Leo capitalization and higher retail spend could be modest capex growth drivers next year.

Gen14 automated fulfillment centers are expected in 2028 with 7 sites pending. They are 2 floors and 1.0-1.4mn sq ft vs 4-6 floors and 2.3-4.0mn sq ft for Gen11/Gen12, and focus on smaller sortable items.
Gen14 average headcount is roughly 1,000 vs ~2,430 for Gen11 and ~1,310 for Gen12. Gen12 already uses robots to pick 65% of SKUs. The stated goal is moving the same volume with a tenth of the labor.

Early ASCS (Amazon Supply Chain Services) feedback is positive, with rates 20-25% below UPS/FDX. MWPVL sees little competitive B2B impact and sees Amazon broadening ASCS toward an end-to-end 3PL offering.

Amazon Logistics is the largest US parcel carrier and expects ~8.0bn packages in 2026 vs 6.67bn in 2025 and 6bn in 2024. Amazon-related USPS and UPS volumes are expected to fall ~800mn and ~525mn packages respectively.

MWPVL expects gradual share loss for USPS/UPS/FDX as Amazon grows from 592 delivery stations toward ~950 by 2030. B2B and reverse logistics remain harder to penetrate because of limited pickup capability and commercial-delivery complexity.
National LTL carriers are seen as relatively insulated: Amazon has fewer than 30 LTL cross docks vs ~300 needed for a scaled national network.
A $1/hr average wage increase raises cost per package by ~3.4%, while a $1 y/y increase in gas costs adds ~1.3%. Fuel rose from $3.25/gal to $4.34/gal over the past year.
MWPVL estimates shipping cost per unit is down 16% since 4Q21, helped by inbound and regionalization efforts, and expects less delivery cost improvement ahead, with automation the key lever.

MWPVL expects a pilot of fully automated delivery stations (Project Tetromino) in 2028, five sites in 2029 and 10 more in 2030, starting at the largest of the 592 US stations, with sorting rates potentially 2.5x existing stations. Amazon is adding robot manufacturing capacity in Austin, TX.

MWPVL estimates Amazon and WFM 2025 food volumes at ~$59bn, 18% of Walmart's ~$321bn. Opening stores is seen as the key lever for profitable grocery, with potential AutoStore integration at future grocery superstores.

BofA maintains Buy and a $317 price objective, viewing Amazon retail as a key beneficiary of AI and robotics-driven automation that improves delivery efficiency and speed and drives share gains vs online retail.

market_movers.rationale: BofA maintains Buy and a $317 PO, citing AI and robotics-driven automation improving delivery efficiency and speed and driving share gains vs online retail.

macro_indicators.reading: $4.34/gal, up from $3.25/gal over the past year
macro_indicators.interpretation: A $1 y/y increase in gas costs adds ~1.3% to cost per package, a smaller effect than wage inflation.

risk_factors: Competition from cloud providers and big box retailers including Walmart.
Rising AWS infrastructure costs that pressure free cash flow.
Agentic AI usage that could pressure direct traffic and high-margin ad revenues.
Stock volatility tied to margin trends, which could increase with economic uncertainty.
